summary: The study describes the use of ozone-based atomic layer deposition (ALD) to deposit Al2O3 on single-layer graphene for dual-gated devices. The process involves a seed layer functionalization at 25 °C using TMA and O3, followed by additional ALD at 200 °C. The ALD process is shown to produce a high-quality dielectric with minimal defects and good electrical properties, including a high dielectric constant, low hysteresis, and low leakage current. The study highlights the importance of temperature control in minimizing defects and maintaining the integrity of the graphene layer.
evidence: We present characteristics of dual-gated graphene devices with an Al2O3 gate dielectric formed by an O3-based atomic-layer-deposition process. Raman spectra reveal that a O3 process at 25 °C on single-layered graphene introduces the least amount of defects, while a substantial number of defects appear at 200 °C. This graphene device with O3-based Al2O3 dielectric demonstrates a heterojunction within the graphene sheet when applying VTG and VBG and possesses good dielectric properties with minimal chemical doping, including a high dielectric constant, low hysteresis width, and low leakage current and a carrier mobility of 5000 cm2/V s at 25 °C in ambient.
